newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end sharply lower due to selling by investors.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end sharply lower due to selling by investors.

text.p: *Key June JGB futures ended sharply lower due to selling of cash bonds by investors, traders said. *Traders said there was widespread talk that life insurers, trust banks and city banks had sold long-term JGBs. *Sharp rise in Tokyo share prices was also negative for JGBs.

"What I'm concerned about is a rumour that...(investors such as)...trust banks may be considering shifting investment away from bonds and toward stocks. If that is true, JGBs will probably fall further," the trader said.
The June ended at 125.03, down sharply from Monday's close of 125.36.
In the Tokyo stock market, the key Nikkei 225 average ended at 19,151.12, up 480.75 or 2.57 percent from Monday's close.
Tokyo financial markets were closed for a national holiday on Tuesday.
JGBs were boosted in the early morning by an overnight rise in U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
Such gains were quickly erased, however, due to investors' selling of cash bonds, they said.
Traders said JGBs recovered somewhat in mid-afternoon, due to rumours that investors had bought back cash JGBs. But they said the upside was capped by the firmness in share prices.
There was talk that an agricultural financial institution had bought cash JGBs on dips, a brokerage house trader said.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.350 percent as of 0647 GMT, up from Monday's close of 2.295 percent.
The selling by investors was probably due to the lingering effects of Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co's business suspension on Friday, traders said.

"The current low interest rate policy has been blamed for low returns on life insurers' investments, and there has been speculation in the market that interest rates may have to be raised to rectify the situation," a city bank trader said.
The Finance Ministry ordered Nissan Life to halt all business except for the servicing of current customers on Friday.
